title: PTE21CSchema
description: SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. Shared definitions for every file in public/data (SPEC §5). TypeScript types in src/data/types.ts are generated from this file; edit here, then run `npm run gen:types`.

Unit.description: The units table (SPEC §5.2). Stored units are fixed per field; display conversions live in src/physics/units.ts. "" means dimensionless. Å³ / a.u. (a₀³) for polarizabilities; s⁻¹ for Einstein coefficients; mg/kg and mg/L for abundances in rock and sea water; t/yr and USD/kg for production; ° and kPa for crystal-cell angles and the pressure of a measurement.

Quantity.description: A number with its unit and source. `unc` is the standard uncertainty in the same unit, when the source gives one; 0 means exact by definition. `text` keeps the exact decimal where `value` (an IEEE double) would lose digits.

text.description: The source's own decimal text, when a double cannot hold every digit (clock frequencies).

doi.description: DOI of the primary paper, where `source` is a collective key such as primary_literature.

arxiv.description: arXiv identifier of the paper, where it has no DOI yet.

Missing.description: An absent value, always with a reason (SPEC §2.2). Never 0, never a bare dash.

Interval.description: IUPAC interval standard atomic weight [low, high]. `conventional` is the single value IUPAC publishes for display, itself a sourced Quantity (SPEC §2.1: no number without a source).

Configuration.description: Ground-state electron configuration. `measured` is the reference configuration from NIST ASD; where NIST has none (Z ≥ 109) it is a published prediction and `flag` is "predicted". `aufbau` is generated by the Madelung rule. Both in noble-gas notation, subshells ordered by n then l.

doi.description: DOI of the primary paper, where `source` is a collective key such as primary_literature.

GroundTerm.description: Ground level. `term` is NIST's designation, e.g. "2S1/2", "1G*4" (* = odd parity), "(1/2,1/2)0". S and L are present only for LS coupling. For Z ≥ 109, where NIST has no data, a relativistic prediction flagged "predicted".

coupling.description: LS: a term symbol; jj: (j1,j2)J, as NIST gives for Pb; J: NIST gives only J.

doi.description: DOI of the primary paper, where `source` is a collective key such as primary_literature.

HyperfineHeadline.description: Ground-state hyperfine splitting of the reference isotope (SPEC §5.1).

attribution.description: The attribution line the licence requires, ready to show.

ImageRef.description: A vendored photograph (SPEC §12): 800 px and 320 px WebP, resized only, with full credit (SPEC §15.4).

ElementFlags.description: Boolean maps. A flag whose curated source table does not exist yet is omitted, never defaulted to false.

ElementIndexEntry.description: One entry of public/data/index.json — tile-level data, kept small.

retrieved.description: UTC date of the cached raw response used for this build (fetched sources only).

LayoutCell.description: Grid position in the shared 32-column coordinate space (SPEC §7.2). col 1–32, row ≥ 1; label positions may use row 0 / spare columns as margins.

LayoutFile.description: public/data/layouts/{id}.json, produced by tools/build_layouts.py. Components read positions from here and never compute them.

Discovery.description: Discovery year from tools/curated/history.toml (which resolves disagreements between PubChem and the IUPAC reports) or PubChem; elements known since antiquity have no year.

axis.description: across: along a period, left to right; down: down a group.

ArrowTrend.description: A classic monotone trend (SPEC §8.1), drawn only in layouts with periods and groups.

Heatmap.description: A numeric field shown as a colour scale (SPEC §8.2). `field` names an index.json field, or `computed:zAlpha` for a value the app computes.

quantity.description: energy and temperature follow the unit setting.

CategoricalMap.description: A categorical map (SPEC §8.3). The pipeline assigns every element a class; the app only draws it.

TrendsFile.description: public/data/trends.json, produced by tools/build_trends.py from tools/curated/trends.toml.

ImagePlaceholder.description: An honest placeholder (SPEC §12.5): no free photograph of the element exists or was found. The app draws the card; nothing is stored as an image.

text.description: The sentence the card shows, values from IAEA.

mode.description: IAEA decay-mode code, e.g. B-, EC+B+, A, SF, IT, B-N, P.

Isotope.description: One nuclide's ground state (IAEA LiveChart, from ENSDF and AME). Bulk numbers carry the file's source.

halfLifeText.description: IAEA's own value, unit and operator, e.g. '> 1.0E26 y'.

jp.description: Spin-parity as ENSDF gives it; brackets mark tentative assignments.

LevelLabel.description: Lower or upper level of a line, as NIST classifies it; fields NIST leaves empty are omitted.

SpectralLine.description: One line: wavelength in nm (medium as the file says), NIST relative intensity (comparable only within one species), Einstein coefficient A_ki in s⁻¹; lower/upper are absent for unclassified lines.

linesInWindow.description: Lines NIST lists in the window.

kept.description: Lines kept in this file: the strongest, up to the SPEC §10.8 cap.

SpectraFile.description: public/data/spectra/{Z}.json (SPEC §10.8): visible lines of the neutral atom and the singly charged ion.

lines.description: Every kept line of every species, by wavelength.

flag.description: NIST's [ ] and ( ) markers on the level energy.

LevelsFile.description: public/data/levels/{Z}.json (SPEC §10.8): the lowest levels of the neutral atom and its ionization limit.

Citation.description: A dated milestone with the paper that reports it.

Eigenvalue.description: Orbital eigenvalue of the neutral atom (NIST SRD 141), in eV.

srs.description: A secondary representation of the second.

isotopeUses.description: Isotopes in biology and medicine (SPEC §10.10), our own words with a source per row. A is omitted when the use is not isotope-specific (gadolinium contrast agents).

toxicity.description: Curated toxicity notes, where a cited source supports one. Absent means no curated note, not 'safe'.

iarc.description: IARC carcinogen classifications of element-related agents; the group comes from the fetched IARC list.

Chemistry.description: Chemistry & bonding (SPEC §10.9): how the element bonds, how it reacts with air, water and acids (our own words, each with its source), well-known compounds, one compound per common oxidation state, and Shannon's ionic radii of its common ions.

oxidationNote.description: What to know about the oxidation states where examples are few or none.

pubchemCid.description: PubChem compound record of the elemental substance (where the HSDB and CAMEO notes are).

sources.description: Where the record holds nothing but Missing notes: the sources those notes rest on.

ChemistryBonding.description: How the atoms of the element itself hold together.

cid.description: PubChem CID whose molecular formula the build checked.

ChemistryIonicRadius.description: Shannon's effective ionic radius of one ion in one coordination (SPEC §10.9).

coordination.description: Coordination number as Shannon writes it: Roman numeral, SQ square planar, PY pyramidal.

ElementDetailFile.description: public/data/elements/{Z}.json: per-panel detail, loaded when the sheet opens (SPEC §5, §10). Sections are keyed by panel slug.

solar.description: Proto-solar mass fraction (dimensionless), Lodders et al. 2025.

solarLogEps.description: Present-day solar-system abundance on the astronomers' log scale, A = log10(N/N_H) + 12 (dex, stored with unit "").

abundanceByMass.description: The four abundances on one scale for the log-scale bars: mg/kg, i.e. parts per million by mass. Derived in tools/build_physical.py from `abundance` (sea water taken as 1 kg per litre; the body amount divided by the 70 kg reference adult); each note says how.

placeLocation.description: Where the discovery place is, from the gazetteer named in tools/curated/places.toml (SPEC §10.11).

prose.description: Our own 60–120-word text (tools/curated/prose/{Z}.md): what it is, one surprising fact, one quantum fact.

MetrologyFile.description: public/data/metrology.json: every clock and standard frequency, every SI role, and the timeline of the second (SPEC §10.6).

CosmicOrigin.description: Share of the element made by each process when the Solar System formed (SPEC §10.7), read off Fig. 39 of Kobayashi, Karakas & Lugaro (2020): an approximation, flagged as such. Keys with zero share are omitted; the shares sum to 1.

recycled.description: Processes whose share in the figure is material those stars returned to space in their winds, not material they made (e.g. AGB stars for thorium and uranium, which their slow neutron captures cannot reach).

CrystalStructure.description: Room-temperature crystal structure from one COD entry (SPEC §10.4); gases and liquids as low-temperature solids, flagged.

ThermalProperties.description: Thermal properties of the element (SPEC §10.4). Molar heat capacity C_p at 25 °C and 1 bar, from the CRC Handbook, in J/(mol·K): per mole of atoms, or per mole of molecules where `formulaAtoms` is given (the diatomic gases and halogens).

formulaAtoms.description: Atoms in the formula unit the value refers to (2 for H₂, N₂, O₂, F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, I₂); absent = per mole of atoms.

UseNote.description: One bullet of what the element is used for, in PTE-21C's own words, with its source (tools/curated/uses.toml).

Allotrope.description: A form of the pure element (tools/curated/allotropes.toml); `standard` marks the reference form at 25 °C and 1 bar.

share.description: Per cent of the ECHA notifications that give this statement, as PubChem aggregates them.

GhsHazards.description: GHS classification of the elemental substance (SPEC §10.4), from its PubChem compound record: the EU harmonised classification where one exists, otherwise PubChem's aggregation of the ECHA C&L notifications with the most reports. Pictograms are drawn by PTE-21C from their codes.

name.description: Short name of what it warns of (tools/fetch_pubchem_ghs.py).

notClassified.description: The classification says the substance does not meet the GHS hazard criteria.

cid.description: PubChem compound ID of the elemental substance.

CoverageFile.description: Per-field coverage over the 118 elements (SPEC §6.4, §13.1), written by tools/report.py for the About page.

note.description: Why the rest are missing, where the data records no reason itself.

ColourMatchingFile.description: public/data/cie1931.json: the CIE 1931 2° colour-matching functions x̄, ȳ, z̄ at 5 nm from 380 to 780 nm (SPEC §11.6), from the pipeline.

WorldMapFile.description: public/data/worldmap.json: the land outline behind the discovery map (SPEC §10.11), simplified from Natural Earth 1:110m land (public domain). Rings of [lon, lat] in degrees, equirectangular.

RelativityFile.description: public/data/relativity.json: where relativity changes chemistry, and where the periodic table ends (SPEC §10.5), from tools/curated/relativity.toml.

RelativityNote.description: One element whose chemistry relativity changes, in our own words, with its paper.

RelativityLimit.description: Where the periodic table would end for a finite nucleus (the point-nucleus limit Z = 1/α is computed from CODATA in the app).
